title: Should You Block Your Ex After You Get Married? The Answer Might Reveal More About Your Heart Than Your Phone
paragraphs:
Should You Block Your Ex After You Get Married? The Answer Might Reveal More About Your Heart Than Your Phone
One message. One memory. One unlocked door. Sometimes the greatest threat to a marriage doesn't begin in a bedroom—it begins with a notification.
There are moments that seem harmless until they aren't.
A late-night memory that appears on your screen because an algorithm remembered what your heart was trying to forget.
Most affairs do not begin with a kiss.
And curiosity, left unguarded, often becomes compromise.
If you're married, should you block your ex?
But perhaps Scripture invites us to ask an even deeper question.
Why are you still leaving the door open?
This is not ultimately about technology.
It is about the condition of the heart.
The Bible never specifically commands, "Block your ex on social media."
Social media did not exist in the first century.
But the God who inspired Scripture understands human hearts better than every psychologist who has ever lived.
The Bible consistently teaches us not merely to avoid sin but to flee the environments where temptation grows.
Not see how close you can get without falling.
Because sometimes the most spiritual thing you can do...
When Potiphar's wife repeatedly tried to seduce him, Genesis never says Joseph stayed to explain himself.
"...he left his garment in her hand and fled and got out of the house."
Joseph valued holiness more than appearances.
Some people today worry more about looking rude than protecting their marriage.
Joseph wasn't worried about looking rude.
He was worried about honoring God.
Marriage is not merely a legal agreement.
"Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh."
Your heart is meant to cling to your spouse.
Jesus later repeats this passage in Matthew 19 and adds:
"What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate."
God Himself yoked husband and wife together.
Why then would we voluntarily keep emotional ropes tied to former relationships?
Not every former relationship is sinful.
Not every former boyfriend or girlfriend is dangerous.
The issue is not merely who they are.
The issue is what happens inside your heart when their name appears.
Do conversations become emotional hiding places your spouse knows nothing about?
"The heart is deceitful above all things."
Our hearts often lie to us before anyone else does.
That's why wisdom builds fences long before disaster arrives.
"Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life."
מִכָּל־מִשְׁמָר נְצֹר לִבֶּךָ (mikkol mishmar netzor libbekha).
Notice what Solomon does not say.
He does not say guard your reputation.
He does not say guard your image.
Sometimes blocking someone is not an act of hatred.
It is an act of stewardship.
"If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away."
He was using powerful imagery to teach radical holiness.
Remove whatever repeatedly pulls your heart away from God.
If an old relationship keeps whispering to your emotions...
If memories repeatedly weaken your commitment...
Holiness has always been more valuable than convenience.
Biblical love is not endless accessibility.
Even Jesus sometimes withdrew from people.
The Apostle Paul instructs believers in Ephesians 5:15–16:
"Look carefully then how you walk... making the best use of the time."
Perhaps the deeper issue is not whether you should block your ex.
If your spouse read every conversation you've had with your ex, would your spouse feel safer...
If secrecy is required to preserve the relationship, that relationship probably should not exist.
Scripture repeatedly calls believers into the light.
The Greek word for "walk" is περιπατῶμεν (peripatōmen).
Perhaps your spouse has no idea.
But that is never the Gospel.
Because the Bible is not merely the story of faithful people.
It is the story of a faithful Savior.
The Samaritan woman carried the weight of broken relationships.
Yet Jesus rewrote every story surrendered to Him.
"Where sin increased, grace abounded all the more."
If your marriage needs repentance, repent today.
If boundaries need rebuilding, rebuild them today.
If conversations need ending, end them today.
If accounts need blocking, block them today.
Boundaries simply honor the Savior who values your covenant.
Marriage reflects Christ and His Church.
Paul says in Ephesians 5 that earthly marriage points toward a far greater reality.
Jesus has never abandoned His Bride.
Our marriages become living sermons when they reflect that same faithfulness.
Perhaps someone reading this has been quietly carrying old emotional attachments for years.
This is not an invitation to guilt.
It is an invitation to freedom.
You do not have to keep feeding yesterday what God has already called you to leave behind.
Sometimes obedience looks as simple as pressing one button.
Not because your ex is necessarily evil.
But because your spouse deserves your undivided covenant.
Someone in your family, a friend, or another couple may need this biblical encouragement before a small compromise becomes a devastating wound.
Even more importantly, you'll gain ongoing access to deeper discipleship content designed to help believers grow in biblical wisdom, spiritual maturity, and unwavering faith.
The strongest marriages are not those that never faced temptation—they are the ones that continually chose Jesus over every competing affection.
